question: Visualize patient transitions between disease stages (I, II, III, IV) across three time points (T1, T2, T3) using a Sankey diagram. Flow width should be proportional to the number of patients making each transition.

files.eval_guideline: Sankey diagram must show patient transitions between disease stages across T1, T2, and T3 with flow widths proportional to patient counts; color scheme and node ordering may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Both files have the identical filename stage_transition_sankey.png and PNG image format. The name directly corresponds to the requested Sankey diagram of patient disease-stage transitions across T1, T2, and T3.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires the diagram to depict stage transitions across T1, T2, and T3 with flow widths proportional to patient counts, while allowing different colors and node orders. Semantic comparison assesses these visual requirements without requiring pixel-level agreement.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images show the same Sankey diagram of patient transitions among disease stages I–IV across T1, T2, and T3. Their node sizes, transition connections, and relative flow widths agree. The candidate explicitly labels counts consistent with the reference geometry: T1 stage totals are 38, 41, 29, and 12; T2 totals are 31, 40, 32, and 17; and T3 totals are 28, 36, 35, and 21. T1→T2 flows are I→I 25, I→II 10, I→III 3; II→I 4, II→II 28, II→III 9; III→I 2, III→II 2, III→III 20, III→IV 5; and IV→IV 12. T2→T3 flows are I→I 25, I→II 6; II→I 3, II→II 30, II→III 7; III→III 28, III→IV 4; and IV→IV 17. Both conserve the cohort of 120 patients and convey identical patterns of stage persistence, improvement, and progression. The candidate adds numerical flow labels, stage totals, time-point headings, and a source-stage color legend, improving quantitative readability without changing the scientific content. Differences in typography, spacing, and color shades are cosmetic.
